title: Measurement and analysis of idiopathic and neurogenic scoliosis with a 3D body scanner
summary:
Scoliosis refers to a three-dimensional deformity of the spine, which is defined by a lateral curvature of at least 10° in frontal view and a rotation of the vertebral body around the vertical axis.
Idiopathic and neurogenic scoliosis typically manifest during the growth phase. The etiology of idiopathic scoliosis has not yet been conclusively clarified. Neurogenic scolioses, on the other hand, are due to underlying neurological diseases.
In patients with cerebral palsy, neuromuscular scoliosis often develops as a result of muscular imbalance, which can occur in early childhood and lead to loss of sitting and trunk balance. Neurogenic scolioses in particular show rapid progression. It is therefore essential to diagnose it as early as possible and to monitor its progress regularly and closely in order to initiate suitable treatment as early as possible.
The use of non-invasive methods to monitor the progression of so-called idiopathic and neurogenic scoliosis in patients with cerebral palsy without the use of ionizing radiation therefore appears promising for reasons of radiation exposure, as is the case with X-rays of the spine.

interventions.name: Development of X-ray-free methods to reduce radiation exposure in children with spinal curvature in cerebral palsy and idiopathic scoliosis. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with neurogenic and idiopathic scoliosis will be included in the study. In the case of idiopathic scoliosis, patients will be included until growth is complete. In the case of neurogenic scoliosis, observation times are necessary beyond the completion of growth.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients with scoliosis due to age-related degenerative changes
